units.text: **Alucita pyrczi Ustjuzhanin & Kovtunovich, sp. nov.**
units.label: Alucita pyrczi Ustjuzhanin & Kovtunovich, sp

units.text: [https://zoobank.org/46B56C3C-9FD0-4C42-B2A3-D3B6FB64F72A](https://zoobank.org/46B56C3C-9FD0-4C42-B2A3-D3B6FB64F72A)
**Type material. Holotype** • ♀, (NECJU 230701), Cameroon, Bamboo Camp, 350 m a.s.l., Mount Cameroon, 4.0879°N, 9.0505°E, 12–20.XII.2014, lgt. V. Maicher, Sz. Sáfián, Š. Janeček, R. Tropek.
units.label: Type material

units.text: **Differential diagnosis.**
units.label: Differential diagnosis

units.text: Externally, Alucita pyrczi closely resembles Alucita lidiya Ustjuzhanin & Kovtunovich, 2018 (known so far only from the male, also collected at Bamboo Camp) but can be distinguished by the presence of a pale orange medial band on its hind wings, the orange band on its fore wings being half as wide, and a larger wingspan.
units.label: Differential diagnosis

units.text: In terms of female genitalia, A. pyrczi shares similarities in the structure of antrum and the shape of papillae anales and apophyses with Alucita molliflua (Meyrick, 1927) (Figs 24, 25).
units.label: Differential diagnosis

units.text: However, these species are clearly differentiated by the structure of the ductus, the position of the ductus seminalis, and the absence of signa in the bursa copulatrix.
units.label: Differential diagnosis

units.text: **External characters.** The head and thorax are covered with appressed darkgrey scales, while the tegulae appear white.
units.label: External characters

units.text: Labial palpi are dark grey on the outside, with white scales on the inner side, and are twice as long as the longitudinal eye diameter.
units.label: External characters

units.text: The third segment is short and white, with scattered tiny brown scales.
units.label: External characters

units.text: The antenna is yellowish white.
units.label: External characters

units.text: The wingspan measures 18 mm.
units.label: External characters

units.text: The fore wing is brown with a distinct orange medium band and is lightened with yellowish white scales at the base.
units.label: External characters

units.text: The hind wings are noticeably paler than the forewings and feature a pale orange medial band.
units.label: External characters

units.text: The lobes of the hind wings have dark-brown and orange spots of scales submarginally.
units.label: External characters

units.text: The fringes on the hind wings are whitish apart from sections of dark-brown hairs around the medial band and submarginal spots, and the distal half of the costa of the first lobe of the hindwing is dark brown.
units.label: External characters

units.text: The hind legs are pale-yellow.
units.label: External characters

units.text: **Female genitalia.** The papillae anales are narrow and elongated.
units.label: Female genitalia

units.text: The posterior apophyses are shorter than the anterior apophyses.
units.label: Female genitalia

units.text: The antrum is wide and goblet-like, sclerotised.
units.label: Female genitalia

units.text: The ductus between the ductus seminalis and antrum
units.label: Female genitalia

units.text: is narrow and short. The ductus widens significantly at the junction with the ductus seminalis and narrows at its entrance to the bursa copulatrix.
The bursa copulatrix is rounded, and no signa are present.
**Distribution.** The species was found in Cameroon only.
units.label: Distribution

units.text: **Flight period.** The species was collected in December.
units.label: Flight period

units.text: **Etymology.** The species is named in honour of the Polish lepidopterist Tomasz Wilhelm Pyrcz, who contributed significantly to the collection and study of butterflies and moths in many parts of the world, including Cameroon.
units.label: Etymology

units.text: **Differential diagnosis.**
units.label: Differential diagnosis

units.text: Alucita sroczki shares a mottled greyish brown wing colouration with Alucita seychellensis (T.B.
units.label: Differential diagnosis

units.text: Fletcher 1910) (illustrated in Ustjuzh anin and Kovtunovich 2016) and Alucita megaphimus (Hering, 1917) (Figs 6–8).
units.label: Differential diagnosis

units.text: However, it can be distinguished from these species by the darkened terminal
units.label: Differential diagnosis

units.text: <details> <summary>natural_image</summary>
<details> <summary>natural_image</summary>
band present on all wings and by its larger size.
The most reliable distinguishing feature lies in the male genital structure.

While the general structure of the male genitalia is reminiscent of A. seychellensis, A. sroczki has narrower valves, a shorter gnathos, and a set of complex sacculus structures with serrated spiky forms, as well as a narrower aedeagus.
In the female genitalia, the new species differs from A. seychellensis and A. megaphimus in the deep V-shaped notch on the outer edge of the antrum.
**External characters.** The head, thorax, and tegulae are covered with clinging grey-brown hairs.
units.label: External characters

units.text: Labial palpi are dark-grey and measure 2.5–3 × the longitudinal eye diameter.
units.label: External characters

units.text: The third segment is thin, long, and belted basally and apically with narrow white scales.
units.label: External characters

units.text: The antennae are dark brown.
units.label: External characters

units.text: The wingspan ranges from 16 to 20 mm (holotype 18 mm).
units.label: External characters

units.text: All wings exhibit a greyish brown colouration, with four and six distinct pale transverse zigzag bands on the fore wing and hind wing, respectively.
units.label: External characters

units.text: The wings are noticeably darkened distally.
units.label: External characters

units.text: The fringe on the lobes of all wings features alternating portions of pale yellow and dark brown hairs.
The hind legs are pale yellow.
**Male genitalia.** The uncus is simple, long, and medially narrowing, with a widened distal end that bears a small notch.
units.label: Male genitalia

units.text: The gnathos is slightly shorter than the uncus and narrow, tapering to an acute apex.
units.label: Male genitalia

units.text: The gnathos arms are short and wide.
units.label: Male genitalia

units.text: The valves are simple and short, measuring half the length of the uncus.
units.label: Male genitalia

units.text: The distal portion of the sacculus is expanded as a forked structure.
units.label: Male genitalia

units.text: The outer portion of this fork is narrower, internally serrated and terminating in an acute and slightly inwardly bent apex.
units.label: Male genitalia

units.text: The inner portion of the fork is wider and finger-like, also serrated on the inside.
units.label: Male genitalia

units.text: The basal portion of the sacculus is wide, with a globular sclerotised formation covered with tiny sharp needles.
units.label: Male genitalia

units.text: The anellus arms are long, equal in length to the gnathos, and wide at the base, gradually narrowing.
units.label: Male genitalia

units.text: The saccus is slightly elongated and caudally rounded.
units.label: Male genitalia

units.text: The aedeagus is straight, basally widened, and 1.5 × longer than the uncus.
units.label: Male genitalia

units.text: The cornutus is needle-like, distinctive, and occupies most of the aedeagus.
units.label: Male genitalia

units.text: **Female genitalia.** The papillae anales are narrow and elongated.
units.label: Female genitalia

units.text: The posterior apophyses are long and thin, approximately equal in length to the anterior apophyses.
units.label: Female genitalia

units.text: The antrum is tubulate and sclerotised, with a narrow V-shaped notch on the outer edge.
units.label: Female genitalia

units.text: The ductus is very short, slightly shorter than the antrum, and the ductus seminalis passes from the confluence of the ductus into the bursa.
units.label: Female genitalia

units.text: The bursa is oval and very large, featuring two narrow ribbon-like signa.
units.label: Female genitalia

units.text: **Distribution.** The species was found in Cameroon only.
units.label: Distribution

units.text: **Flight period.** The species was sampled in April and October.
units.label: Flight period

units.text: **Etymology.** The species name is a noun in apposition.
units.label: Etymology

units.text: It is named in honour of the curators from NECJU, Ewelina Sroka and Karolina Sroka, who crucially contributed to the processing of the abundant moth material collected on Mount Cameroon and several other Afrotropical localities.
units.label: Etymology

units.text: The name ’sroczki’ refers to the nickname commonly used for the twin sisters.
units.label: Etymology

units.text: **Note.** Previously, Ustjuzhanin and Kovtunovich (2017) erroneously synonymised A. megaphimus with A. seychellensis.
units.label: Note

units.text: Later, PU and VK re-examined their characters in more detail, and therefore we consider Alucita megaphimus (Hering, 1917), stat. rev., as a separate species.
units.label: Note

**Differential diagnosis.**
units.label: Differential diagnosis

units.text: In the male genitalia, the new species exhibits great similarity to Alucita escobari Ustjuzhanin & Kovtunovich, 2018, from which it differs in the more reduced notch in the top of the uncus and in the caudally acute saccus.
units.label: Differential diagnosis

units.text: In contrast, in A. escobari the notch on the top of the uncus is clearly expressed, triangular, and the saccus is caudally smooth, oval, and not acute.
units.label: Differential diagnosis

units.text: Additionally, these two moth species are clearly distinct externally.
units.label: Differential diagnosis

units.text: In the female genitalia, the new species closely resembles Alucita besongi Ustjuzhanin & Kovtunovich, 2018 and Alucita janeceki Ustjuzhanin & Kovtunovich, 2018.
units.label: Differential diagnosis

units.text: From the former, it differs in the oval, elongated bursa copulatrix and the absence of small signa in it, while in A. besongi the bursa copulatrix is pear-like, its surface covered with tiny signa.
units.label: Differential diagnosis

units.text: From the latter, the new species differs in the shape of the bursa copulatrix and the antrum, in the new species the bursa copulatrix narrows caudally, while in A. janeceki, it has a rounded base.
units.label: Differential diagnosis

units.text: The antrum in the new species has a narrow V-shaped notch on the outer edge, while in A. janeceki the notch is wide.
units.label: Differential diagnosis

units.text: From both species, the new species differs in the very long posterior apophyses, in A. besongi and A. janeceki the anterior and posterior apophyses are equal in the length.
units.label: Differential diagnosis

units.text: Furthermore, the male genitalia of the new species are clearly different from those of A. besongi and A. janeceki.
units.label: Differential diagnosis

units.text: **External characters.** The head, thorax, and tegulae are white.
units.label: External characters

units.text: Labial palpi are pale-yellow and measure twice the longitudinal eye diameter.
units.label: External characters

units.text: The antennae are yellowish white.
units.label: External characters

units.text: The wingspan ranges from 9 to 12 mm (holotype 11 mm).
units.label: External characters

units.text: The wings are pale yellow, mottled, with alternating white and yellowish brown portions of scales.
units.label: External characters

units.text: All lobes of the wings have small dark spots of scales on tips.
units.label: External characters

units.text: The fringe on all lobes of the wings has alternating white and pale brown portions of hairs.
units.label: External characters

units.text: The hind legs are white.
units.label: External characters

units.text: **Male genitalia.** The uncus is long, distally extended, and apically with a poorly visible notch.
units.label: Male genitalia

units.text: The gnathos is slightly shorter than the uncus and apically acute.
units.label: Male genitalia

units.text: The gnathos arms are wide and slightly shorter than the gnathos itself.
units.label: Male genitalia

units.text: The valves are wing-like and apically have a bundle of thin needle-like setae.
units.label: Male genitalia

units.text: The anellus arms are wide, straight, and equal in length to the gnathos.
The saccus is elongated and forms a narrow triangle, with an acute tip.
The aedeagus is almost straight, obliquely cut apically, and without cornuti.
**Female genitalia.** The papillae anales are narrow and elongated.
units.label: Female genitalia

units.text: The posterior apophyses are very long and thin.
units.label: Female genitalia

units.text: The antrum is sclerotised, with a narrow V-shaped notch on the outer edge.
units.label: Female genitalia

units.text: The ductus is very short, slightly shorter than the antrum, and the ductus seminalis extends distally inside the bursa copulatrix.
units.label: Female genitalia

units.text: The bursa copulatrix is oval, elongated, and noticeably narrows at the end, with numerous longitudinal long ribs inside.
units.label: Female genitalia

units.text: **Distribution.** The species was found in Cameroon.
units.label: Distribution

units.text: **Flight period.** The species was collected in May and from October to December.
units.label: Flight period

units.text: **Etymology.** The species is named after Fako, the local name of Mount Cameroon, which is the type locality of the species.
units.label: Etymology

units.text: The name aims to emphasise the importance of the area and encourage the protection of the species’ habitats.
units.label: Etymology

units.text: **Differential diagnosis.**

units.text: In terms of wing colouration, the species somewhat resembles Alucita mischenini Ustjuzhanin & Kovtunovich, 2018, but it differs in the length of the apical dark-brown portion of scales on the first and second lobes of the fore wing.
units.label: Differential diagnosis

units.text: In the new species, the portion on the second lobe is twice as long as that on the first lobe, while in A. mischenini it is equal to or even shorter than that on the first lobe.
units.label: Differential diagnosis

units.text: In the male genitalia, there is also a similarity to A. mischenini, but in the new species, the saccus has a distinct triangular notch caudally, and the aedeagus has an ordered arrangement of needle-like cornuti distally.
units.label: Differential diagnosis

units.text: In contrast, in A. mischenini the notch is absent on the saccus, and the cornuti in the aedeagus are tiny and chaotically disorganised.
units.label: Differential diagnosis

units.text: **Flight period.** The species was collected in April.
units.label: Flight period

units.text: **Etymology.** The species is a noun in apposition. ‘Erzayi’ is a word in the Bakweri language, which is the dominant local language in the Mount Cameroon region, and it translates to “feather”.
units.label: Etymology

units.text: This corresponds with the appearance of many-plumed moths’ feather-like characteristic wing lobes.
units.label: Etymology

units.text: **Differential diagnosis.**
units.label: Differential diagnosis

units.text: The wing colour of this species slightly resembles Alucita jana Ustjuzhanin & Kovtunovich, 2020, but it can be distinguished by the widened distal band on the fore wing, whereas in A. jana it narrows at the fourth-fifth lobe.
units.label: Differential diagnosis

units.text: Additionally, A. sokolovi has a band in the medial portion of the wing, which is absent in A. jana.
units.label: Differential diagnosis

units.text: The labial palpi of the new species are 3 × longer than the longitudinal eye diameter, compared to only 1.5 × in A. jana.
units.label: Differential diagnosis

units.text: In the male genitalia, the structure of the aedeagus and the shape of the gnathos of A. sokolovi slightly resemble Alucita bokwango Ustjuzhanin & Kovtunovich, 2020.
units.label: Differential diagnosis

units.text: However, A. sokolovi can be differentiated by its uncus, which is widened on the top, and the wide oval apical portions of the valves, while in A. bokwango the uncus is narrow throughout its length, and the valves’ apices are less widened.
units.label: Differential diagnosis

units.text: **External characters.** The head has white shiny scales.
units.label: External characters

units.text: The thorax and tegulae are covered with pale brown clinging scales.
units.label: External characters

units.text: The labial palpi are wide, long, \~ 3 × as long as the longitudinal eye diameter, white inside and brown outside.
units.label: External characters

units.text: The third segment is isolated and apically acute.
units.label: External characters

units.text: The antennae are yellowish brown, and the scape is wide and flattened.
units.label: External characters

units.text: The wingspan is 17–18 mm (holotype 17 mm), and the wings are pale brown.
units.label: External characters

units.text: There are two clearly expressed wide brown bands on the fore wings, distally and basally.
units.label: External characters

units.text: The fore wings are
units.label: External characters

units.text: apically framed with a white subapical zigzag.
The hind wings are noticeably paler than the fore wings, with a brown band widening towards the last three lobes.
There are bundles of brown hairs on the lobes, both distally and basally, with white fringes between them.
The hind legs are pale yellow.
**Male genitalia.** The uncus is long, noticeably exceeding the gnathos in length, and is distally slightly widened with a small apical notch.
units.label: Male genitalia

units.text: The gnathos is narrow and apically acute.
units.label: Male genitalia

units.text: The valves are long and membranous, apically smoothly forming a wide oval shape.
units.label: Male genitalia

units.text: The anellus arms are thin and straight.
units.label: Male genitalia

units.text: The saccus is caudally oval.
units.label: Male genitalia

units.text: The aedeagus is short, almost straight, and has two spiky cornuti.
units.label: Male genitalia

units.text: **Differential diagnosis.**
units.label: Differential diagnosis

units.text: The mushroom-like antrum and elongated crest-like signum of this species bear similarity to Alucita ectomesa (Hering, 1917) (illustrated in Ustjuzhanin and Kovtunovich 2016), but it can be distinguished by the wider ductus, the round bursa copulatrix, and numerous tiny spiky signa present in it.
units.label: Differential diagnosis

units.text: Additionally, the unique colouration of the wings sets A. hirsuta apart from all other African Alucitidae species.
units.label: Differential diagnosis

units.text: **External characters.** The head, thorax, and tegulae are dark brown.
units.label: External characters

units.text: The labial palpi are short, slightly longer than the longitudinal eye diameter.
units.label: External characters

units.text: The antennae are brown. The wingspan is 14 mm, and the wings have a reddish brown appearance.
units.label: External characters

units.text: The lobes of all wings bear protruding tousled dark-brown hairs, especially dense on the first two lobes of the fore wings, creating the appearance of a shaggy moth.
units.label: External characters

units.text: There are narrow, poorly visible pale longitudinal bands on all wings.
units.label: External characters

units.text: The fringe on all wings ranges from pale to dark brown.
units.label: External characters

units.text: The hind legs are yellow.
units.label: External characters

units.text: **Female genitalia.** The papillae anales are narrowly triangular in shape.
units.label: Female genitalia

units.text: Both the posterior and anterior apophyses are of equal length, thick, and straight.
units.label: Female genitalia

units.text: The antrum is wide and mushroom-like.
units.label: Female genitalia

units.text: The ductus is wide, corrugated, and strewn with narrow strands.
units.label: Female genitalia

units.text: The ductus seminalis passes from the middle of the ductus.
units.label: Female genitalia

units.text: The bursa copulatrix is round, with a robust crest-like signum located in the upper part of the bursa, near the confluence of the ductus.
units.label: Female genitalia

units.text: Numerous tiny spiky signa densely cover the entire surface of the bursa.
units.label: Female genitalia

units.text: **Distribution.** The species was found in Cameroon only.
units.label: Distribution

units.text: **Flight period.** The species was collected in October.
units.label: Flight period

units.text: **Etymology.** The species name is derived from Latin ’hirsute’ (shaggy, bristly, hairy).
units.label: Etymology

units.text: It refers to the appearance of the adult moth, with tousled protruding dark-brown hairs on the wings, reminiscent of a hairy and shaggy moth.
units.label: Etymology

units.label: Type material

units.text: **Differential diagnosis.**
units.label: Differential diagnosis

units.text: The yellow wing colour of this species resembles Alucita compsoxantha Meyrick, 1924, but it can be distinguished by the differences in the position of the bands.
units.label: Differential diagnosis

units.text: In the male genitalia, A. potockyi shares similarities with Alucita tesserata (Meyrick, 1918) in the short uncus widening towards the apex and in the saccus shape, but it clearly differs in the apically tapered gnathos, long narrow valves and the long aedeagus that exceeds the genital structure in its length.
units.label: Differential diagnosis

units.text: In comparison, A. tesserata has a gnathos that strongly widens apically, short and wide valves, and a noticeably smaller aedeagus relative to the genital structure (see Ustjuzhanin et al. 2020a for the genitalia illustration).
units.label: Differential diagnosis

units.text: **External characters.** The forehead is covered with white clinging scales, while the nape bears protruding yellow-brown hairs.
units.label: External characters

units.text: The thorax and tegulae are yellowish brown.
units.label: External characters

units.text: The labial palpi are short, \~ 1.5 × as long as the longitudinal eye diameter, with the third segment acute and framed with brown scales.
units.label: External characters

units.text: The antennae are yellow, with only the basal area above the scape adorned with dark-brown scales.
units.label: External characters

units.text: The wingspan measures 14 mm, and the wings have a yellowish brown colouration.
units.label: External characters

units.text: There is a narrow white band medially on the fore wings (potentially even more bands can be present, but it is difficult to distinguish them clearly on the single available specimen of a mediocre quality), and alternating brown and yellowish portions of scales are present in the distal half of the fore wings.
units.label: External characters

units.text: The wings’ basal areas are covered with brown scales.
units.label: External characters

units.text: The hind wings are slightly paler than the fore wings, with alternating brown and yellow portions of scales along all lobes.
units.label: External characters

units.text: The fringe on all wings is yellow, and the hind wings appear pale-yellow.
units.label: External characters

units.text: **Male genitalia.** The uncus is short, widening apically.
units.label: Male genitalia

units.text: The gnathos is robust, sharply narrowing apically.
units.label: Male genitalia

units.text: The valves are narrow, long, and poorly sclerotised.
units.label: Male genitalia

units.text: The gnathos arms are short and narrow-triangular.
units.label: Male genitalia

units.text: The anellus arms are thin, long, straight, and apically form axe-shaped extensions.
units.label: Male genitalia

units.text: The saccus is caudally oval.
units.label: Male genitalia

units.text: The aedeagus is long, slightly longer than the genital structure, and bears a series of tiny transverse spiky cornuti distally, along with two big needle-like cornuti positioned along the aedeagus medially.
units.label: Male genitalia

units.text: **Distribution.** The species was found in Cameroon only.
units.label: Distribution

units.text: **Flight period.** The species was collected in October.
units.label: Flight period

units.text: **Etymology.** The species is named after the Czech lepidopterist Pavel Potocký Sr., in appreciation of his long-term support with moth preparation and identification in various projects of RT’s research group.
units.label: Etymology
